No, Originally whenever these are purchased they are imported, and due to the asinine government regulations on firearms imports, they are imported in "sporting" configuration. This means the trigger group is moved rearward, and a shotgun style stock is attached. Converting it means moving the trigger group forward, to the original location, and installing a different stock. there's some dremeling involved, in both the receiver and trigger group, and drilling new holes for the pins. I installed a tapco double hook trigger set in mine, and after some polishing and tweaks here and there, it operated perfectly, even on that cheap-o wal-mart birdshot.

Patience is a virtue with something like this.

Yeah, dunno, I don't usually post negative replies but when I think 'shotgun on steroids' I think more like the AA-12. Full auto 12ga, drum magazine. The UTS-15 is just a regular pump action shotgun. It's a bullpup so it can be shorter in overall length while still having barrel length, plus it has two mag tubes so capacity is around double your average pump action. There's also the KSG which fits the same general description, there are differences though, like the KSG has two mag tubes that are manually selectable, the UTS-15 automatically alternates. Both seem like a cool feature depending on what you're going for. Straight up capacity, or a switch to change what type of shells you're using.
